Anyone know what the blue shock wave is caused by? Seems to happen when not much else is going on.

We melt radioactively contaminated metal at our facility in a large induction furnace, somewhat similar to what's shown in this video. Prior to charging metal to the bath, it is put through a preheater process where twelve 1 million BTU burners burn away any plastic, rubber, or liquids that might be on the metal, in addition to heating the metal. We do this because of what you see in the video.

Effectively, any liquid or combustible material that reaches the molten bath with flash vaporize, creating a bubble of gas (size dependent on the amount of material vaporized) which then rises rapidly to the surface of the molten metal. The pressure behind this bubble can be pretty large, as the surface tension of liquid metal is far higher than that of water. In addition, any slag that may be on the surface of the bath will prevent the bubble from escaping until the pressure is high enough to break through. When it does, it acts a lot like an explosion, flinging liquid metal everywhere.

The worst is when the combustible has sunk to the bottom prior to hitting the liquid (typically because it is contained inside a metal container like a steel drum). The speed of the rising bubble pushes more metal up and out. Combine all of that with the radioactive particles inherent to our process, and you have a big, dangerous mess.

TL;DR - Don't put things that burn or boil in a molten metal bath.
